name: EGFR (epidermal growth factor receptor)
summary: Activating EGFR kinase-domain mutations define an oncogene-addicted subset of non-squamous NSCLC, enriched in never/light smokers and in patients of East Asian ancestry, and predict benefit from EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitors.
biology: EGFR is an ErbB-family receptor tyrosine kinase. Activating mutations in exons 18-21 destabilise the inactive kinase conformation, producing ligand-independent signalling through RAS-MAPK, PI3K-AKT and JAK-STAT pathways. Classical sensitising mutations (exon 19 deletions and exon 21 L858R) increase sensitivity to ATP-competitive inhibitors relative to wild-type EGFR, creating the therapeutic window exploited by EGFR TKIs. Exon 20 insertions generally alter the drug-binding pocket and confer primary insensitivity to most first- to third-generation EGFR TKIs.
alterations: Uncommon mutations: G719X (exon 18), L861Q (exon 21), S768I (exon 20) and compound mutations
Exon 20 insertions (generally TKI-insensitive; distinct targeted options)
Acquired T790M gatekeeper mutation (resistance to first/second-generation TKIs)
Acquired C797S/C797G (resistance to covalent third-generation TKIs)
EGFR amplification and kinase-domain duplication (less common)

methods: Plasma ctDNA NGS or PCR-based assays
testing.specimen: Formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded tumour tissue (biopsy, resection or cytology cell block); plasma ctDNA as a complementary or initial approach
testing.notes: Broad NGS panels are preferred over single-gene PCR because many hotspot PCR assays miss exon 20 insertions and uncommon variants. A negative plasma result does not exclude a mutation and should prompt tissue testing. Testing is recommended in non-squamous NSCLC and in squamous NSCLC with atypical clinical features, and before adjuvant therapy in resected early-stage disease.

predictiveRelevance: Classical sensitising mutations predict benefit from EGFR TKIs (osimertinib being the preferred first-line backbone in most guidelines, alone or in combination strategies) and identify patients who derive limited benefit from single-agent PD-(L)1 blockade. Uncommon mutations show variable TKI sensitivity, with afatinib and osimertinib having the most supportive data. Exon 20 insertions are targeted with amivantamab-based therapy. EGFR status also guides adjuvant TKI use after resection and consolidation strategies after chemoradiotherapy in stage III disease.
resistance: On-target: T790M after first/second-generation TKIs; C797S (in cis or trans with T790M) and other tertiary mutations (L718Q, G724S) after osimertinib
Bypass signalling: MET amplification (most common bypass after osimertinib), HER2 amplification, KRAS/NRAS/BRAF mutations, PIK3CA mutations
Acquired oncogenic fusions (RET, ALK, BRAF, FGFR3)
Histological transformation to small-cell carcinoma (often with RB1 and TP53 loss) or squamous carcinoma
Re-biopsy (tissue and/or plasma) at progression is recommended to identify actionable mechanisms
cnsConsiderations: Brain metastases are common in EGFR-mutant NSCLC. Osimertinib and lazertinib have good CNS penetration and intracranial activity, which has made them preferred over first-generation agents for patients with or at risk of CNS disease. Leptomeningeal disease is a recognised pattern of progression.
